issues.description: Collapsing working and walking into one state changes the DFS state machine without verification.
issues.detail: The old machine distinguished 'children pushed' from 'currently descending', and push() reads that label for cycle detection. Merging them is likely correct but is a behavioral change disguised as a rename. Verify the cycle-handling branch still behaves identically with one label doing two jobs, and document the merged state's invariant.

issues.description: Sorted marker now only set when yield returns true, a semantic change not called out.
issues.detail: Previously s.state[k]=sorted ran unconditionally after pop; now it runs only on yield success. This couples correctness to the deferred clear and changes early-termination semantics. Probably fine since the iterator is dead and defer wipes state, but the state-machine change needs explicit justification in the commit message or a comment.

issues.description: Cleanup lifetime moved from Sort() entry to defer without documenting the contract change.
issues.detail: Original code cleared state at entry; new code clears in defer on iterator completion. Better choice (memory released sooner, cheaper reuse) but a contract change. If Sort() is called and the returned iter.Seq is never invoked, prior state persists. Add a one-line spec on the Sorter struct stating preconditions, postconditions, and the reuse invariant.

issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: PR title says 'Fix state reuse' but adds no test. A Sort()-twice test on the same Sorter with different graphs, asserting results plus len(s.stack)==0 and len(s.state)==0 after iteration, would lock in the fix. Without it the next refactor silently reintroduces the bug.

issues.description: Updated comment contains typos ('visisted', 'if its') in load-bearing documentation.
issues.detail: The comment is the de-facto contract for the state field and explains why each node is visited twice. 'visisted' -> 'visited', 'if its' -> 'if it's'. Comments explaining the algorithm deserve the same care as the code, especially when they are the only written spec of the ADT's state machine.

issues.description: Three independent fixes squashed into one diff; intent of clear()+reslice unstated.
issues.detail: The patch bundles (1) state collapse, (2) stack-reset bugfix (s.stack[0:] was a no-op; clear()+s.stack[:0] is correct), and (3) yield-ordering change. Split for bisectability. Also state whether clear() is for GC of pointer elements or superstition — one line of intent beats two lines of ceremony.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR moves in the right direction — collapsing working/walking, fixing the s.stack[0:] no-op, and deferring cleanup are all sound — but lands as needs-work. The state-machine collapse and the yield-conditional sorted marker are behavioral changes presented as cleanup, with no written contract on the Sorter ADT and no regression test for the reuse bug the PR claims to fix. Three independent fixes are squashed into one diff, and the load-bearing comment has typos. Split the patches, add a Sort()-twice test, document the new reuse invariant, and fix the comment.
